title: 29.25 · Motional voltage along a rod
given: Rod a→b points up-right, length 0.300 m. It moves down-right perpendicular to itself at 5.00 m/s through B = 0.450 T into page.
find: Find voltage magnitude, higher-potential end, internal E and positive end; then voltage for motion along the rod or out of the page.

steps.title: Find voltage and electric field
steps.math: |\Delta V|=BLv=(0.450)(0.300)(5.00)=0.675\ \mathrm V\\E=vB=(5.00)(0.450)=2.25\ \mathrm{V/m}\\q\mathbf E+q\mathbf v\times\mathbf B=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad\mathbf E=-\mathbf v\times\mathbf B

steps.title: Check the other motions
steps.math: \mathbf v\parallel\text{rod}:\quad(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)\cdot\boldsymbol\ell=0\\\mathbf v\parallel\mathbf B:\quad\mathbf v\times\mathbf B=0\\\Delta V=0\quad\text{for both alternate motions}

answer: 0.675 V; b positive and higher; E = 2.25 V/m toward a; both alternate motions give 0 V.
check: For along-rod motion the magnetic force is perpendicular to the rod; for motion parallel/antiparallel to B it vanishes.

title: 29.26 · Loop leaving a field
given: Loop 0.300 m wide × 0.400 m tall moves right at 0.0200 m/s out of a region with B = 1.25 T into page.
find: Find emf when fully inside, partly inside and fully outside.

steps.title: Evaluate the three positions
steps.math: \text{Fully inside: }dA/dt=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad\mathcal E=0\\\text{During exit: }|dA/dt|=hv\\|\mathcal E|=(1.25)(0.400)(0.0200)=0.0100\ \mathrm V\\\text{Fully outside: }\Phi=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad\mathcal E=0

check: During exit induced current is clockwise to reinforce the diminishing inward flux. Use the 0.400 m side transverse to motion.

title: 29.29 · Sliding rod and energy conservation
given: Rod length 0.500 m slides right at 7.50 m/s along closed rails; B = 0.800 T into page; circuit resistance 1.50 Ω. Top rod end a, bottom b.
find: Find induced emf, rod current direction, required external force, and mechanical/electrical powers.
answer: 3.00 V; 2.00 A b→a; external force 0.800 N rightward; both powers 6.00 W.
check: The magnetic force on the rod is leftward. External mechanical work supplies the resistive heat.

title: 30.11 · Polarity of a decreasing-current inductor
given: L = 0.260 H; current runs from b to a (right-to-left) and decreases at 0.0180 A/s.
find: Find induced emf and higher-potential end.
answer: 4.68 mV; a is higher than b.
check: The inductor acts as a source while returning stored magnetic energy; a is at higher potential.
